arxiv-2309-10451.title: The coupled-cluster self-energy
arxiv-2309-10451.creator: Christopher J. N. Coveney, David P. Tew
arxiv-2309-10451.description: Abstract Coupled-cluster and Green’s function theories are highly successful in treating many-body electron correlation and there has been significant interest in identifying and leveraging connections between them. Here we present a diagrammatic definition of the irreducible coupled-cluster self-energy that directly embeds coupled-cluster theory within the framework of many-body field theory.

arxiv-2402-11261.title: Isotypical equivalence of periodic Abelian groups
arxiv-2402-11261.creator: Elena Bunina
arxiv-2402-11261.description: Abstract . In this paper we give invariants that characterize isotypically equivalent Abelian periodic groups. Also, we describe types of standart tuples of elements in these groups. As the particular case we prove that two Abelian p p -groups with separable reduced parts are isotypically equivalent if and only if their divisible parts and their basic subgroups are elementarily equivalent.

arxiv-2403-17495.title: Quantum Optimization for the Future Energy Grid: Summary and Quantum Utility Prospects
arxiv-2403-17495.creator: Jonas Blenninger, David Bucher, Giorgio Cortiana, Kumar Ghosh, Naeimeh Mohseni, Jonas Nüßlein, Corey O’Meara, Daniel Porawski, Benedikt Wimmer
arxiv-2403-17495.description: Abstract In this project summary paper, we summarize the key results and use-cases explored in the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) funded project “Q-GRID” which aims to assess potential quantum utility optimization applications in the electrical grid.

arxiv-2408-12200.title: An image-based blind search for Fast Radio Bursts in 88 hours of data from the EoR0 Field, with the Murchison Widefield Array
arxiv-2408-12200.creator: Ian Kemp, Steven Tingay, Stuart Midgley, Daniel Mitchell
arxiv-2408-12200.description: Abstract This work is part of ongoing efforts to detect Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) in a spectral window below 300 MHz. We used an image-based method based on the pilot study of Tingay et al. 2015, scaled up via massively parallel processing using a commercial supercomputer. We searched 87.

arxiv-2503-23383.title: ToRL : Scaling Tool-Integrated RL
arxiv-2503-23383.creator: Xuefeng Li Haoyang Zou Pengfei Liu
arxiv-2503-23383.description: Abstract We introduce ToRL (Tool-Integrated Reinforcement Learning), a framework designed to train large language models (LLMs) to autonomously utilize computational tools through scaling reinforcement learning directly from base models (i.e., models without post-training). Unlike approaches based on supervised fine-tuning, ToRL enables models to discover optimal strategies for tool utilization via unrestricted exploration. Experiments with Qwen2.

arxiv-2503-24117.title: Organizations, teams, and job mobility: A social microdynamics approach inspired by a large US organization
arxiv-2503-24117.creator: Bryan Adams, Valentín Vergara Hidd, Daniel Stimpson, Miesha Purcell, Eduardo López
arxiv-2503-24117.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bryan Adams, Valentín Vergara Hidd, Daniel Stimpson, Miesha Purcell, Eduardo López. Most of the modeling approaches used to understand organizational worker mobility are highly stylized, using idealizations such as structureless organizations, indistinguishable workers, and a lack of social bonding of the workers.

pmc-10696044.title: Defect modes in defective one dimensional parity-time symmetric photonic crystal
pmc-10696044.creator: Tiecheng Wang, Yong Niu
pmc-10696044.description: The introduction of defect layers into one-dimensional parity-time (PT) symmetric photonic crystals gives rise to resonances within the photonic bandgaps. These resonances can be effectively explained by our generalized temporal coupled mode theory. The scattering properties and dispersion relation of defect modes exhibit distinct characteristics compared to conventional one-dimensional Hermitian photonic crystals with defect layers.

pmc-11387075.title: Public and Clinician Perspectives on Ventilator Withdrawal in Vegetative State Following Severe Acute Brain Injury: A Vignette Survey
pmc-11387075.creator: Shin Hye Yoo, Jung Lee, In Gyu Song, So Yeon Jeon, Min Sun Kim, Hye Yoon Park
pmc-11387075.description: BackgroundThe vegetative state (VS) after severe acute brain injury (SABI) is associated with significant prognostic uncertainty and poor long-term functional outcomes. However, it is generally distinguished from imminent death and is exempt from the Life-Sustaining Treatment (LST) Decisions Act in Korea.

pmc-11489375.title: Optimizing the effect of heat treatment on the mechanical properties (tensile Strength and hardness) of Hyphaene Thebaica nut; A machine learning and Taguchi approach
pmc-11489375.creator: Bassey Okon Samuel, Abdulmumin Akoredeley Alabi, Shehu Abba Lawal, Enejor Peter, Tanimu Kogi Ibrahim
pmc-11489375.description: The demand for innovative and sustainable biomaterials in healthcare and biotechnology has fueled the need for advancements in its engineering performance. However, the limited properties of biomaterials without the integration of synthetic reinforcements or supports pose a challenge. Consequently, there is a growing necessity for the development of full cycle eco-friendly materials.

pmc-11676955.title: Synthesis and Degradation of the Phytohormone Indole-3-Acetic Acid by the Versatile Bacterium Paraburkholderia xenovorans LB400 and Its Growth Promotion of Nicotiana tabacum Plant
pmc-11676955.creator: Paulina Vega-Celedón, Diyanira Castillo-Novales, Guillermo Bravo, Franco Cárdenas, María José Romero-Silva, Michael Seeger
pmc-11676955.description: Plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) play a role in stimulating plant growth through mechanisms such as the synthesis of the phytohormone indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). The aims of this study were the characterization of IAA synthesis and degradation by the model aromatic-degrading bacterium Paraburkholderia xenovorans LB400, and its growth promotion of the Nicotiana tabacum plant.

pmc-12509898.title: Translesion Synthesis DNA Polymerase Gene Expression Is Impacted by Age and IGF-1 in Epidermal Human Skin
pmc-12509898.creator: Stanley D. Rider, Madison S. Owens, Craig A. Rohan, Jeffrey B. Travers, Michael G. Kemp
pmc-12509898.description: Regions of sun-exposed skin are prone to carcinogenesis in geriatric individuals and exhibit a reduced ability to remove mutagenic UV photoproducts from DNA. To determine whether geriatric skin may be more reliant on translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases to replicate unrepaired UV photoproducts, we examined the expression of TLS polymerases in the epidermis of young and geriatric individuals.

pmc-12562093.title: Differential Association of Serum TSH with Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Risk by Autoimmune Thyroiditis Status
pmc-12562093.creator: Lu Yu, Hanyu Wang, Xiao Chen, Yuhan Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Yang Chen, Yuxin Yu, Siqi Wang, Yu Wang, Zixuan Wang, Lejing Xie, Hui Sun, Sonam Kumari
pmc-12562093.description: Background: While elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is a known risk factor for differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), it remains unclear whether autoimmune thyroiditis (AT) modifies this association. Clarifying this interaction is critical for personalized risk assessment and TSH suppression therapy. Methods: This study performed a retrospective analysis including 2425 participants who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules.

pmc-12606780.title: A Systematic Review of the Cost-Effectiveness of Screening Modalities for Breast Cancer in European Countries
pmc-12606780.creator: Zacharoula Sidiropoulou, Vasco Fonseca
pmc-12606780.description: Simple SummaryBreast cancer screening programs vary widely across European countries, and decision-makers need clear information about which approaches offer good value for money. This review examined 23 studies from across Europe to understand which breast cancer screening methods are cost-effective.

pmc-12661228.title: mHealth Use, Preferences, Barriers, and eHealth Literacy Among Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Survey Study
pmc-12661228.creator: Christopher Kretzschmar, Johannes Knitza, Robert Pietschner, Raja Atreya, Markus Friedrich Neurath, Till Orlemann
pmc-12661228.description: BackgroundMobile health (mHealth), defined as health care facilitated by mobile devices, offers a promising strategy for enhancing disease management and treatment for patients with chronic conditions. However, there is limited information about how patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) use mHealth and their digital preferences.

pmc-12712531.title: New RCTs Advance Incremental Dialysis With Clinically-Guided HD and HDF-Based Prescriptions
pmc-12712531.creator: Mariana Murea, Andrea K Viecelli
pmc-12712531.description: equency is rooted in tradition and logistical convenience rather than scientific evidence. By contrast, incremental dialysis individualizes treatment by incorporating RKF into the prescription, typically starting with lower frequency (once- or twice-weekly sessions) and escalating to thrice-weekly as clinical status or RKF decline dictates.

pmc-13111542.title: A novel and efficient method for producing high-purity single protoplast-derived isolates of Plasmodiophora brassicae
pmc-13111542.creator: Ling Cao, Qilin Chen, Jinghe Wang, Hao Hu, Fengqun Yu
pmc-13111542.description: Plasmodiophora brassicae, a root-infecting protist, causes the devastating clubroot disease of cruciferous crops worldwide. Field populations of this pathogen often consist of multiple strains, leading to inconsistent experimental results and unreliable resistance classification in breeding programs. The extremely low infection success rate associated with single resting spore inoculation has limited the generation of genetically uniform single spore-derived isolates (SSIs).

pmc-13155577.title: Significance of RGS13 expression in lupus B cells
pmc-13155577.creator: Tomoya Nakajima, Koji Kitagori, Sohei Funakoshi, Mirei Shirakashi, Ryosuke Hiwa, Hideaki Tsuji, Shuji Akizuki, Ran Nakashima, Akio Morinobu, Hajime Yoshifuji
pmc-13155577.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesB cells play important roles in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. In this study, we explored the proteins preferentially expressed in SLE B cells, especially double-negative 2 B (DN2B) and age-associated B cells (ABCs), and analysed their functions.MethodsWe used our previously reported dataset to identify the mRNAs preferentially expressed in SLE B cells and confirmed their expression in each B cell subset via flow cytometry.

pmc-13211028.title: Vegetation-Mediated Soil Organic Carbon Differentiation and Carbon Sequestration Strategies in a Typical Wetland of the North China Plain
pmc-13211028.creator: Zonglin Shi, Yan Wang, Xiaoshuang Li, Na Zhang, Sisi Li, Yue Wang, Hongjun Lin, Yuhong Dong, Hongju Zhou, Dayong Wu, Man Cheng
pmc-13211028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Soil organic carbon (SOC) responds rapidly to vegetation changes, and exploring SOC sequestration mechanisms under different vegetation types is critical for optimizing wetland carbon sink functions. This study investigated the abiotic and biotic mechanisms driving SOC stability across four typical vegetation types (reed marsh, woodland, farmland, and wasteland) in the 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm soil layers of Hengshui Lake wetland.

pmc-13532761.title: Usage and impact of global biodata resources
pmc-13532761.creator: Carla Cummins, Heidi Imker, Charles E Cook, Guy Cochrane, Shanfeng Zhu
pmc-13532761.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). MotivationBiodata resources constitute a critical, large-scale, and globally distributed infrastructure underpinning life science research, yet their organic growth has hindered efforts to quantify key indicators needed to justify sustainable support, including usage, impact, and interdependencies. Here, we present an updated Global Biodata Coalition inventory alongside a Total Resource Usage (TRU) dataset that integrates this inventory with two complementary literature-derived sources: data citations and informal resource name mentions extracted from full-text articles using a fine-tuned machine learning model.

pmc-13607188.title: Early Postoperative Remodeling of the Exhaled Volatilome Following Curative Surgery for Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13607188.creator: Elizaveta Tyukanova, Zaki Fashafsha, Aleksandr Suvorov, Anastasia Fatyanova, Valeriy Ponomarev, Artemiy Silantyev, Denis Khlusov, Akmalbek Otabekov, Yaroslav Krasnov, Maksim Volgin, Bogdan Tkachenko, Albina Zubayraeva, Sergey Efetov, Philipp Kopylov, Marina Sekacheva
pmc-13607188.description: Background: Exhaled volatile organic compounds (VOCs) may provide a non-invasive readout of biological changes in colorectal cancer (CRC). We characterized early postoperative changes in the exhaled volatilome after curative CRC surgery and explored a multivariable VOC signature associated with clinical state.

pmc-13646671.title: Daily Heat Stress Induces Donor‐Side Limitation of PSI Via Downregulation of the Cyt b6f Complex
pmc-13646671.creator: Laura Laihonen, Tutta Tomberg, Linda Vuorijoki, Lauri Nikkanen, Paula Mulo, Marjaana Rantala
pmc-13646671.description: The rapidly warming climate is driving increasingly frequent and intense heat waves worldwide, posing major challenges to plant metabolism and growth. Despite the central role of photosynthesis in plant growth, the effects of prolonged heat stress on the primary reactions of photosynthesis remain poorly understood.
